tools.name: get_latest_version
tools.description: Resolves the latest published version of a Maven Central artifact (any groupId:artifactId — Java, Kotlin, or Scala library). Call this first when you only know the artifact but not the version: the version it returns feeds into every other tool here that takes a concrete version. By default it returns the latest release, sorted by Maven version order and skipping pre-releases; set `includePreReleases` to true to get the newest version of any kind (milestone, RC, beta...), e.g. when a class or method you are looking for is missing from the latest release. Works against the live Maven Central catalog — no local install, build tool, or repository checkout required.

includePreReleases.description: Optional, default false. When true, also consider pre-releases (milestones, RCs, betas, alphas, snapshots), e.g. to find a new API that only exists in a milestone. When false, returns the latest release (or the newest pre-release if the artifact has no release at all).

inputSchema.description: A Maven Central artifact (groupId and artifactId) whose latest version to resolve.

tools.name: get_javadoc_index
tools.description: Fetches the rendered Javadoc/Scaladoc index page for a specific Maven Central artifact version, converted to plain text/markdown. Useful for orienting yourself in an unfamiliar library: it lists the top-level packages, modules, and (for Scaladoc) often a curated overview. Use this before drilling into specific symbols. Works against the live Maven Central catalog — you do not need to download the javadoc jar.

inputSchema.description: A fully-qualified Maven Central artifact coordinate: groupId, artifactId, and version.

tools.name: list_javadoc_symbols
tools.description: Enumerates the public API a library documents — classes, interfaces, traits, objects, enums, and annotations — for a Maven Central artifact version. Each entry includes the fully-qualified class name (`fqn`) and a `link` that can be passed to get_javadoc_symbol to read the rendered API documentation. Use this to answer 'which classes/types does library X have?' or 'find classes related to <topic>' — it is the fastest way to list the API by name without reading code. Prefer this over list_source_files whenever you only need class/type names. Pass `filter` (e.g. a class name) to get only the matching entries: large libraries list hundreds of symbols, so filtering saves a lot of context when you are looking for one type. Only if this returns NotFoundError because no javadoc jar was published, or an empty list because the published jar is empty, fall back to list_source_files. Works against the live Maven Central catalog with no local install, build, or checkout required.

filter.description: Optional. Only return symbols whose fully-qualified name contains this text (case-insensitive; several space-separated terms must all match), e.g. "PolymorphicTypeValidator" or "judge Builder". Omit to list every symbol.

inputSchema.description: A Maven Central artifact version whose documented symbols to list, optionally narrowed by name.

tools.name: get_javadoc_symbol
tools.description: Reads one Javadoc/Scaladoc page from a Maven Central artifact, already converted to plain text/markdown so you don't have to parse HTML. Pass the `link` value returned by list_javadoc_symbols. Navigation and links to external sites are stripped; the links that remain point at other pages of the same jar and can be passed back as `link` to follow them. Use this when you need to know what a class, method, or field does and what its parameters mean for any library on Maven Central — without downloading or unzipping the javadoc jar yourself.

link.description: The relative path/link within the jar, as returned by list_javadoc_symbols or list_source_files.

inputSchema.description: A pointer to one documented page or source file inside an artifact's jar.

tools.name: get_source_file
tools.description: Reads one source file from a Maven Central library's sources jar (the `-sources.jar` artifact). Pass the `link` value returned by list_source_files. Use this whenever you need the exact source text of a JVM library — tracing behavior into a dependency, confirming a public API's implementation, finding a definition, or comparing two library versions. Strongly preferred over locating the jar in a local build cache and unzipping it: it works for any Maven Central artifact, no local checkout or build needed. Large files (list_source_files gives each file's `sizeBytes`; over about 20000 bytes) can exceed your tool-output limit: pass `grep` to find the lines you need (each result line is numbered), then `startLine`/`endLine` to read the surrounding code. Without them the whole file is returned.

link.description: The path of the file within the sources jar, as returned by list_source_files.

startLine.description: Optional. First line to return (1-based, inclusive). Omit to start at line 1.

endLine.description: Optional. Last line to return (1-based, inclusive). Omit to read to the end of the file.

grep.description: Optional. Only return lines matching this case-insensitive regex (matched as plain text if it is not a valid regex), e.g. "def apply" or "class .*Codec". Combine with startLine/endLine to search part of the file.

inputSchema.description: One source file inside an artifact's sources jar, optionally narrowed to a line range or to matching lines.

tools.name: list_source_files
tools.description: Lists the raw source files (`.java`, `.kt`, and `.scala`) in a Maven Central artifact version's `-sources.jar`. Each entry's `link` can be passed to get_source_file to read the actual source code, and its `sizeBytes` tells you whether to read the whole file or only part of it (with get_source_file's `grep` or line range). Use this only when you need the implementation — for example, to trace behavior or see how something is wired. To discover which classes exist, or to find classes by topic or name, use list_javadoc_symbols instead; do not use this tool just to enumerate classes. Works against the live Maven Central catalog with no local install, build, or checkout required.

inputSchema.description: A fully-qualified Maven Central artifact coordinate: groupId, artifactId, and version.

tools.name: search_artifacts
tools.description: Finds Maven coordinates from part of a library name: searches the javadocs.dev index of Maven Central artifacts for groupId:artifactId values containing every word of the query (case-insensitive). Use this when you know part of a library name (e.g. "jackson", "zio-http", "netty-codec") and need the exact groupId:artifactId coordinates to feed into the other tools. Query with name fragments only — versions are not part of the match. The same artifactId can be published under several groupIds (e.g. jackson-databind: com.fasterxml.jackson.core for 2.x, tools.jackson.core for 3.x), so check each candidate with get_latest_version. The index only holds artifacts javadocs.dev has already read, so an empty result doesn't mean the artifact doesn't exist: if you know the exact coordinates, check them with get_latest_version. To find the library that contains a class, use symbol_to_artifact instead.

query.description: The text to search for — e.g. a class/type name, a package, or part of a groupId/artifactId.

tools.name: symbol_to_artifact
tools.description: Finds which Maven artifact contains a given Java/Kotlin/Scala class: resolves a class name, nested type (e.g. Outer.Builder), fully-qualified type, or package name to the Maven Central artifacts (groupId, artifactId) that publish it. Matching ignores case and returns every artifact with a symbol whose name contains the query (queries under 3 characters must match a name exactly). If none does, a simple name is matched by close spelling, so a typo still finds the class. A query that is part of a groupId:artifactId returns those artifacts instead. The index covers artifacts javadocs.dev has already read; when it has no match, the result comes from an AI guess checked against the live Maven Central catalog, and those artifacts are indexed for next time. Several artifacts can contain the same simple name (e.g. a Java and a Scala library): check each result rather than assuming the first. Use this when you have a symbol from a stack trace, an import line, or an error message and you need to know which library to look in. From there, chain into get_latest_version, then list_source_files / list_javadoc_symbols to read the code or docs.

query.description: The text to search for — e.g. a class/type name, a package, or part of a groupId/artifactId.
